bullets: How one drop of water travels round and round
slides.heading: The Water Cycle
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we are going to follow a single drop of water on a journey that never ends, and by the end you will be able to tell its whole story.

bullets: Name the four stages of the water cycle in order
Explain what makes the water change at each stage
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud slowly and tell the class: keep these in mind, because our exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these two things.

bullets: This morning there was a puddle outside the classroom
By recess it was gone - where did the water go?
slides.heading: Where did the puddle go?
slides.notes: Ask for a show of hands and take two or three guesses without judging them yet; say: hold on to your idea, because the answer is the first stage of our cycle.

bullets: Liquid water can become an invisible gas called water vapour
Water vapour can cool back into liquid water
The same water goes round and round in a cycle
slides.heading: Water changes state, it never vanishes
slides.notes: Say this part slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: the water changes its form, liquid to gas and back again, but the amount of water stays the same.

bullets: The sun heats the sea, lakes and puddles
Warmed water rises into the air as invisible water vapour
slides.heading: Evaporation: the sun lifts the water
slides.notes: Point at the animation and narrate what is happening: watch the drops rise as the sun warms the sea - that rising is evaporation, and the water is still there, just invisible.

bullets: High up, the air is cold
Water vapour cools and turns back into tiny liquid drops
The tiny drops gather together as a cloud
slides.heading: Condensation: vapour becomes a cloud
slides.notes: Tell them to imagine breathing on a cold mirror: the mist that appears is the same trick - vapour cooling back into tiny drops, and a cloud is billions of those drops together.

bullets: The drops join and grow bigger and heavier
When they are too heavy to float, gravity pulls them down as rain
slides.heading: Precipitation: water falls back down
slides.notes: Ask the class what pulls the rain down, then confirm it: gravity wins once the drops grow too heavy, and scientists give falling water the special name precipitation.

bullets: Rain runs off the land into streams and rivers
Rivers carry the water back to the sea, ready to start again
slides.heading: Collection: water gathers again
slides.notes: Trace the river with your finger as you say: downhill all the way, back to the sea - and tomorrow the sun will lift that very same water again, because the cycle never stops.

bullets: A drop in the sea is warmed by the sun and evaporates
It cools into a cloud, falls as rain on a hill, then flows down a river back to the sea
slides.heading: Worked example: trace one drop
slides.notes: Talk through the journey step by step and name each stage as the drop reaches it; say: notice the drop is never created or destroyed, it only changes form and place.

bullets: Arrange the four stage cards in the order the water travels
Careful - a classmate says the water disappears for good once it evaporates; explain to them why that is wrong
slides.heading: Your turn: put the cycle in order
slides.notes: Give pairs two minutes with the cards, then cold-call one pair and press them on the trap: if the water had really disappeared when it evaporated, where would rain come from?

bullets: Write the four stages in order and one sentence on what drives each change
Finish this sentence and defend it: water does not disappear for good once it evaporates, because ...
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for the word vapour in your last answer - if you can explain where the water hides after it evaporates, you have cracked today's lesson.
